text:
Maya: Quick check — PR #7892 (storage shard routing) is green in CI but blocked on the storage-sharding RFC signoff. RFC: https://redwood.company/rfcs/storage-sharding. @Samir can you take a look? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/7892
Samir: On it. Skimming the RFC now. First question: does the new routing table format require kernel selection changes in the runtime? If so we need a compatibility shim path.
Ben: From my quick read it's mostly additive. We will need a tiny change in routing table serialization (see comment on PR). Not a blocker for rollout, but needs review.
Olivia: Can we have an arch review checklist here so it's easier to sign off? I can do a pass if Samir is busy.
Samir: I'll review by EOD. If it's only the serialization tweak and a fallback, we can merge after a small patch. @Maya can you attach the perf numbers you mentioned?
Maya: Added perf table to the PR description and a microbenchmark gist. Also added a proposed rollout plan (canary -> ramp). Snippet:```
canary:
  percent: [5,25,100]
  duration: 15m
```
CI Bot: CI status — all checks passed. Note: e2e flake in test_shard_rebalance (1 failure, marked flaky).
Ben: That flake is the one I hit yesterday. I'll push a small stabilization fix to the test before merge.
Samir: Reading RFC "compatibility" section now — request adding an explicit fallback policy for older routing versions. Please add as a commit or a follow-up PR against this branch.
Maya: I'll add the fallback policy and unit tests, ETA tomorrow morning.
Olivia: :thumbsup: Sounds good. Once Samir gives arch + compat ack, Ben can merge after canary config is applied.
Maya: Thanks all — I'll update the PR with the fallback and ping here when done. If helpful I can schedule a 10-min sync. @Ben @Samir
